title: Introduce cost-symphony: defaults orchestrator for batching, cache & quant profiles
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safe, opinionated defaults that improve per-token unit economics without surprising latency regressions. This PR adds a new service (cost-symphony) that synthesizes tenant-level batching, KV-cache, and quantization defaults from sampled workload signatures and runtime telemetry. Goals: 1) provide deterministic, auditable defaults for new tenants and rolloutable updates for existing tenants; 2) reduce typical token cost on common web workloads by ~12% without increasing p99 tail latency beyond SLA; 3) expose a dry-run mode and a human-review path for safety-critical accounts. Summary of changes: - New service: redwood/cost_symphony/ with a small runtime that ingests sampled traces and computes a prioritized list of defaults (batch_shape, cache_prefill_policy, quant_profile). Defaults are represented as JSON profiles and versioned in the defaults registry. - Defaults-as-code: introduce a CLI redwood-cli defaults synth that can produce deterministic presets from a captured workload snapshot and upload them as a draft profile. - Safe rollout: server-side rollout controller that supports canary -> tiered rollout across tenant cohorts with automatic rollback on cost/quality regressions. - Offline prober: a synthetic prober that runs simulated inference with candidate defaults against a small, representative sample and computes delta metrics (cost/token, avg latency, p95/p99). - Telemetry and evals: new telemetry keys (symphony.profile_id, symphony.sim.delta_cost, symphony.sim.quality_change) and a lightweight evaluator for detecting hallucination/regression against a canonical prompt set. - Console integration: expose generated draft profiles in the Console defaults UI under "Cost automation -> Suggested defaults" and allow a one-click approve/apply. - Tests and CI: unit + integration tests for the synth algorithm; a deterministic snapshot-based integration test that runs prober comparisons on CI. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: Linear ENG-5421 linked and reviewed - [x] Implementation: core synth, registry, rollout controller - [x] CLI: redwood-cli defaults synth + dry-run - [x] Telemetry + metrics: added to metrics schema - [x] Console surface: draft UI card + apply flow - [x] E2E: prober-based smoke tests - [x] Documentation: docs/ defaults automation guide is included Breaking considerations: Profiles are opt-in by default for existing tenants; new tenants receive a recommended profile but can opt out. Rollouts run with conservative thresholds by default and require explicit enablement for high-SLA tenants. Performance summary: On an internal web-chat workload sample, the synthesized default reduced median cost/token by 12.3% and 95th-percentile token cost by 9.4%; avg latency increased 1.8ms and p99 was unchanged within noise. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, enable draft uploads to staging for two weeks, run prober sweeps, then gradual canary to 5% of tenants. Related work: builds on tenant-warmstart/tenant-prefill work and reuses portions of the sample-cataloger. Links: Linear ENG-5421, ENG-6120 (prober enhancements).

review_comments: Marco Li: Did you consider restricting quant-profile suggestions to only LLM families that we have validated quantizers for? I worry about applying 4-bit suggestions to models not tested.
Priya Desai: Good point — synth now tags profiles with 'validated_model_families' and the rollout controller refuses apply if tenant runs an unsupported model. Added tests for the guard.
Rafael Gomez: The prober should include a tiny canonical prompt set to catch quality regressions; please add a signal for hallucination rate change.
Priya Desai: Added symphony.sim.quality_change and a lightweight BLEU-ish matcher for template-based prompts; documented false-positive modes in the docs.
Anika Schultz: CLI UX: dry-run output should show expected delta metrics and the JSON profile; done, and user can --approve to upload draft.
Jamie Park: Console card looks good but needs tooltip copy on 'expected cost savings' explaining simulation assumptions; updated copy in the last commit.
release_notes: Adds 'Cost Symphony' defaults orchestrator: automated synthesis of batching, cache prefill and quantization presets; CLI synth + dry-run; console UI for suggested profiles; safe rollout/controller with telemetry and prober-based validations. New metrics: symphony.profile_id, symphony.sim.delta_cost, symphony.sim.quality_change.
notes_for_oncall: No immediate oncall changes required. Default rollouts are disabled by default; if enabling for production tenants, monitor symphony.sim.delta_cost and symphony.sim.quality_change for spikes. If quality_change > 0.02 for any canary cohort, rollback the rollout controller for that profile.
